title: Further proof transformations, modal logic, and ordinal analysis
details: Develop sequent-calculus interpolation for equality-free first-order proofs as a separate syntactic treatment from the existing classical Craig interpolation theorem, and extend interpolation to intuitionistic first-order logic. Develop general Herbrand extraction beyond leading existential blocks, with quantified contraction handled explicitly. Extend cut transformations and Harrop extraction to calculi preserving logical equality, establish the required equality-enabled conservativity, and retain the exact existential-witness and name-universe hypotheses. Develop varying-domain Kripke completeness with logical equality or without the current countable-language and countable-name restrictions. For propositional logic, develop quantitative bounds on cut elimination. Strong normalization and confluence need an explicitly specified local natural-deduction reduction relation and proofs for its arbitrary reduction sequences. For constructive arithmetic, prove preservation of the original native HA axioms under Friedman translation, including finite parameter closure and the allowed free-parameter conditions, and establish an appropriate Friedman-based arithmetic conservativity theorem. Develop realizability, numerical existence and disjunction properties, and provably total functions. Primitive recursive arithmetic and ordinal analysis require their own arithmetic-strength arguments; Goodstein termination by ordinal descent does not establish PA unprovability or a Gentzen consistency theorem. Heyting-algebra semantics needs its lattice foundations. Modal logic belongs in its own area.
